name: Quantization

# Quantization


## Overview
Quantization is a lossy [compression](#4-compression.md) technique that maps continuous or high-precision data to a discrete set of values to reduce memory footprint and bandwidth [S1][S2, unofficial]. It solves the problem of storing large volume datasets by reducing bit-depth, typically achieving significant compression ratios (e.g., 4:1 for 32-bit to 8-bit) [S1][S2, unofficial]. It differs from general [scalar quantization](#5726-scalar-quantization.md) by specializing the mapping based on data type (e.g., perceptual color spaces, geometric normal mappings) or by integrating quantization into the [training loop](#4290-training-loop.md) for neural fields, rather than applying a generic linear mapping [S1].

## Shared principles
Not given in the sources.

## Subtopics

### [Attribute Quantization](1912-attribute-quantization.md)
[Attribute quantization](#1912-attribute-quantization.md) reduces the precision of voxel attributes (colors and normals) to lower memory footprint while maintaining perceptual quality [1912-attribute-quantization.md]. It differs from [Scalar Quantization](5726-scalar-quantization.md) and [Uniform Quantization](5855-uniform-quantization.md) by specializing the quantization method based on data type, using perceptually uniform color spaces (CIELAB) and geometric mappings (Octahedron Normal Vectors) rather than generic linear mappings [1912-attribute-quantization.md].

### [Scalar Quantization](5726-scalar-quantization.md)
Scalar quantization (per-block) is a random-access decompression method that reconstructs voxel values on-the-fly from compressed data [5726-scalar-quantization.md]. It solves the problem of storing high-precision volume data by mapping a block of voxels to a local range defined by block-specific minimum and maximum values, allowing for parallel GPU decompression without loading full-resolution data into memory [5726-scalar-quantization.md]. It differs from general scalar quantization by computing range parameters locally per block rather than globally, and from hardware-accelerated block-coding by relying on software-defined linear interpolation formulas [5726-scalar-quantization.md].

### [Uniform Quantization](5855-uniform-quantization.md)
[Uniform quantization](#5855-uniform-quantization.md) is a lossy compression method that maps a continuous or high-bit-depth source domain to a discrete set of indices using evenly spaced intervals [5855-uniform-quantization.md]. It serves as the baseline for volume data compression, reducing memory footprint by representing large raw data values (e.g., 32-bit floats) with a limited number of bits (e.g., 8 bits) [5855-uniform-quantization.md]. Unlike non-uniform or [adaptive quantization](#5858-non-uniform-quantization.md), it does not allocate levels based on data distribution, making it simple to implement but potentially ineffective for data with wide dynamic ranges [5855-uniform-quantization.md].

### [Chroma Subsampling](6512-chroma-subsampling.md)
[Chroma subsampling for volumetric data](#6512-chroma-subsampling.md) reduces the bitrate of color information by lowering the spatial resolution of chrominance components (U, V) while maintaining full resolution for luminance (Y) [6512-chroma-subsampling.md]. It solves the problem of significant color information loss and "grey object" artifacts that occur when direct subsampling is applied to sparse volumetric data at low bitrates [6512-chroma-subsampling.md]. Unlike direct subsampling, it defines one color value for every eight adjacent corners using a median-based approach, preserving color quality better than naive approaches [6512-chroma-subsampling.md].

### [TetSplat Pre-processing and Data Layout](7221-tetsplat-pre-processing-and-data-layout.md)
[TetSplat Pre-processing and Data Layout](#7221-tetsplat-pre-processing-and-data-layout.md) is the method for quantizing scalar field values and packing them into binary bitstrings for efficient storage and transmission within the TetSplat volume rendering system [7221-tetsplat-pre-processing-and-data-layout.md]. It solves the problem of managing large tetrahedral meshes with multiple scalar fields by compressing [hierarchical data structures](#4133-hierarchical-data-structures.md) (Shell and Solid) into a single binary stream [7221-tetsplat-pre-processing-and-data-layout.md]. It sets itself apart from general quantization methods by its specific integration with unbalanced tree traversal pointers and the hierarchical encoding of geometric attributes (normals) alongside scalar data [7221-tetsplat-pre-processing-and-data-layout.md].

### [Differentiable Quantization for Neural Fields](10195-differentiable-quantization-for-neural-fields.md)
[Differentiable Quantization for Neural Fields](#10195-differentiable-quantization-for-neural-fields.md) reduces the memory footprint of 3D [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md) and [neural radiance fields](#4972-neural-radiance-fields.md) by compressing grid values to single bytes during the optimization process [10195-differentiable-quantization-for-neural-fields.md]. Unlike post-training quantization, which causes quality degradation due to mismatch between the optimized model and the rendering engine, this method integrates quantization into the training loop using a straight-through estimator [10195-differentiable-quantization-for-neural-fields.md]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Scalar Quantization](5726-scalar-quantization.md) by ensuring the quantized representation is learned end-to-end, preserving rendering quality while enabling real-time synthesis in unbounded scenes [10195-differentiable-quantization-for-neural-fields.md].

### [Neural Implicit Network Compression](10414-neural-implicit-network-compression.md)
[Neural Implicit Network Compression](#10414-neural-implicit-network-compression.md) (INR) replaces explicit voxel grids with a coordinate-based neural network that maps spatial coordinates directly to field values, serving as simultaneously compressed storage and a queryable data source [10414-neural-implicit-network-compression.md]. Unlike traditional lossy compressors that produce bitstreams requiring full decoding before visualization, INRs allow direct evaluation at arbitrary resolutions [10414-neural-implicit-network-compression.md]. The method sets itself apart by achieving high compression ratios on scalar fields (e.g., 545:1) while maintaining high fidelity, though it typically requires significant training time and lacks native interactive rendering capabilities compared to cached or decompressed alternatives [10414-neural-implicit-network-compression.md].

### Lossy Quantization for Coarsened Patches
Lossy compression for coarsened patches in the bintree hierarchy. Quantization error $q$ is proportional to coarsening error $c$: $q = qc$, where $q$ is a fixed constant usually $< 1$. A single unified error is recomputed and nested for each patch. Quantization levels are restricted to power-of-two multiples of vertical resolution $\Delta z$ for efficient bit-shift implementation. Shift $k$ is calculated as: $k = \lceil \log_2(\epsilon_q / \Delta z) \rceil + 1$ if $\epsilon_q \ge \Delta z$, else $0$. All finest level vertices have zero shift. Vertices classified as boundary (corners $C$, legs $L$, hypotenuse $H$) and interior $I$. Corners stored at full precision. Quantization of original height values (not residuals) ensures adjacent patches agree on shared boundaries [S1].

### HSV Colour Sorting
A technique to preserve colour quality during DXT1 compression by reordering colours based on HSV values [S2, unofficial]. The effectiveness of HSV sorting depends on which component (H, S, or V) is the most frequent in the voxel data’s set of colours [S2, unofficial].

### Interpolation Symmetry Quantization
A method to improve the accuracy of quantized weights by exploiting the symmetry of linear interpolation between segments [S3]. Quantize both $w$ and $1 - w$ using the codebook generated by the scalar quantizer. Keep the representation resulting in the lower error. Store either $(i, j, w)$ or $(j, i, 1 - w)$ in the output stream. Linear interpolation: $(1 - w)s_i + w s_j$, where $(i, j, w)$ is equivalent to $(j, i, 1 - w)$ [S3].

### Position Lattice Quantization
An attempted method to compress Gaussian positions by quantizing them to a lattice structure and embedding positional constraints into the training process [S4]. Fails to compress positions without introducing significant rendering error [S4]. Identified as a future research direction for end-to-end positional compression [S4].

## Background
Quantization is a fundamental technique in data compression, widely used in volume rendering to manage the high memory bandwidth and storage requirements of large-scale volumetric datasets. In the context of volume rendering, it is often employed in conjunction with transform-based compression (e.g., wavelets) or as a standalone method for attribute reduction (colors, normals). The specific applications detailed in the subtopics, such as differentiable quantization for neural fields [10195-differentiable-quantization-for-neural-fields.md] and neural implicit network compression [10414-neural-implicit-network-compression.md], represent recent advancements integrating quantization into the learning process of neural representations. Traditional uniform and scalar quantization remain standard for reducing precision in density fields [5855-uniform-quantization.md][5726-scalar-quantization.md].
